concept_gloss.applicability: İşin hem başkasına bırakılmasını hem de o kişinin temsil yetkisi kazanmasını birlikte anlatan genel karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Devretme işlemini ve bundan doğan temsil ilişkisini birlikte korur.

concept_gloss.text: bir işi başkasına devredip onu kendi adına yetkilendirme

concept_map.definition: Bir işi, kişiyi ya da karar yetkisini başkasına bırakıp o kişiyi kendi adına işi yürütmekle yetkilendirmektir. Kendisine iş bırakılan kişi de bu yetkilendirme uyarınca işi üstlenir.

facets.statement: Bir işin veya kişinin sorumluluğu, yürütülmesi ya da karara bağlanması için başkasına bırakılır.
İşi alan kişi, devreden adına hareket eden yetkili temsilci konumuna gelir.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir işin yürütülmesi veya karara bağlanması açıkça belirli bir kişiye bırakıldığında kullanılır.

error_profile.loses: Yetkilendirilen kişinin devreden adına temsilci oluşunu açıkça söylemez.
error_profile.preserves: İşi başkasının yetki ve kararına bırakma yönünü korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir kişinin belirli bir işi devreden adına yürütme yetkisi kazanması öne çıktığında kullanılır.

error_profile.loses: İşin o kişinin kararına bırakılması yönünü geri planda bırakır.
error_profile.preserves: Yetkili temsilci oluşturma ve onun devreden adına hareket etme yönünü korur.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal başkasına güvenme durumunu değil, işi açıkça ona devredip onu kendi adına yetkili kılma işlemini merkez alır.
identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir işi ya da kişiyi başkasına bırakmayı, işi onun yetki ve kararına bağlamayı ve onu kendi adına görevli kılmayı birlikte anlatır. Verilen dal çerçevesi bu devretme işlemini ve bundan doğan temsil ilişkisini doğru biçimde korur.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: onu birine bırakıp işini ona devretmek
belirli bir iş için onu yetkili kılmak

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, çeşitli çekimli kullanımlarla adlaşmış görev ve temsil biçimlerini ayırır; bunlardan bağımsız, sınırsız bir yalın kök anlamı çıkarmaz.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar devretme, temsil, güvenme ve ilişkili görev alanları bakımından değerlendirildi; yalnızca yetkilendirme sınırını en açık biçimde gösteren üç karşılaştırma yayımlandı.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal, işin devredilmesiyle kurulan yetki ilişkisini anlatır; komşu dal ise bu ilişkinin nasıl kurulduğunu belirtmeden bir kişinin diğerinin yerini almasını merkez alır.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bir işin açıkça devredilmesini ve devralanın bu iş için yetkili kılınmasını gerektirir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Birinin başka birinin yerini almasını anlatabilir; açık bir yetkilendirme işlemi şart değildir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her ikisinde de bir kişi başka biri adına veya onun konumunda iş görür.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalın çekirdeği yetkili kılma ve temsil ilişkisidir; komşu dal bırakma işlemiyle birlikte devredenin karşı tarafa dayanmasını da anlamın parçası yapar.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Başkasını kendi adına işi yürütecek yetkili kişi durumuna getirme yönünü içerir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: İşi başkasına geri çevirmenin yanında ona dayanıp güvenme tutumunu da içerir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dalda da bir iş başka bir kişiye bırakılır.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal işi devredenin yaptığı yetkilendirmeye, komşu dal ise görevi alan kişinin yeterlilik, koruma ve güvence sağlayan işlevine odaklanır.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: İşi başkasına devrederek yetki ilişkisini kuran işlemi anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Devredilmiş işi yeterince yerine getiren, koruyan veya güvence altına alan kişiyi anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal aynı devretme ilişkisinin karşılıklı iki tarafına bağlanır.

branches.source_phrase_ar: وكلته إليك أكله كلة أي فوضته (ayn)؛ سمي الوكيل لأنه يوكل إليه الأمر (maqayis)؛ وكلته بأمر كذا توكيلا والاسم الوكالة (sihah)؛ وكيل الرجل الذي يقوم بأمره (tahdhib)؛ التوكيل أن تعتمد على غيرك وتجعله نائبا عنك (mufradat)

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak çizgisi, bir işin başkasına devredilmesi ve bu kişinin işi devreden adına yürütmekle yetkili kılınmasıdır; görev adı ile görevi üstlenen kişi aynı ilişkinin farklı yönleridir.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه التوكيل والتفويض والوكالة والوكيل الموكول إليه الأمر وما يكل المرء إليه أمره
branches.what_is_not_ar: ليس هو مجرد الاتكال العاجز ولا المواكلة ولا وكال الدابة

concept_gloss.applicability: Kişinin bir işte kendi gücünü yetersiz görüp başka birini güvenilir ve yeterli dayanak saydığı bütün kullanımlara uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Yetersizlik kabulünü, dayanmayı ve güvenmeyi birlikte korur.

concept_gloss.text: kendi yetersizliğini kabul edip başkasına dayanarak güvenme

concept_map.definition: Kişinin bir işte kendi gücünün yetmediğini kabul ederek başka birine dayanması, ona güvenmesi ve işi bakımından onu yeterli görmesidir.

facets.statement: Kişi bir işte kendi yetersizliğini ortaya koyar ve başka birini dayanak edinir.
Dayanak edinilen varlığa güvenilir ve onun işi karşılamaya yeterli olduğu kabul edilir.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir insanın belirli bir işte başka bir insanı dayanak edindiği olağan bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.loses: Kişinin kendi yetersizliğini ortaya koyma yönünü açıkça belirtmez.
error_profile.preserves: Başka birine dayanma ve ona güvenme yönlerini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Güvenin Tanrı'ya yöneldiği ve onun koruyup yeterli olacağı inancının öne çıktığı bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.loses: İnsanlara dayanmayı içeren daha genel kullanım alanını dışarıda bırakır.
error_profile.preserves: Güvenilen varlığı yeterli dayanak sayma yönünü korur.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal birini yetkili temsilci kılmayı değil, kişinin kendi işinde başka bir varlığa dayanıp güvenmesini anlatır.
identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, kişinin bir işte kendi yetersizliğini ortaya koyarak başkasına dayanmasını ve onu güvenilir dayanak saymasını anlatır. Verilen dal çerçevesi, gerek Tanrı'ya gerek bir insana yönelen bu güvenip dayanma ilişkisini doğru biçimde karşılar.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: Tanrı'ya güvenmek ve onun koruyup yeteceğine inanmak

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, Tanrı'ya güvenmeyi bildiren kalıpla kişilere dayanmayı bildiren çekimli kullanımları ayrı bağlamlar olarak korur ve bunları yalın köke genellemez.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar güven, yeterlilik, yardım, devretme ve güçsüzlük sınırları bakımından değerlendirildi; yayımlanan üç ilişki dalın güvenip dayanma çekirdeğini en iyi ayıranlardır.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalın çekirdeği güvenip dayanma tutumudur; komşu dal bu tutuma işi başkasına bırakma veya geri çevirme işlemini de ekler.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Kişinin kendi yetersizliğini ortaya koyup karşı tarafı yeterli dayanak saymasını gerektirir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: İşi açıkça başka birine devretme veya onun hükmüne geri çevirme işlemini içerir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dalda kişi işi bakımından başka birine yönelir ve ona dayanır.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal güven ve yeterlilik kabulünü merkez alır; komşu dal ise dayanmayı yardım alma, başvurma ve seçeneği ona bağlama gibi daha geniş işlevlerle birleştirir.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Kendi yetersizliğini kabul ederek birini güvenilir ve yeterli dayanak sayma yönünü içerir.
neighbor_distinctions.gloss: birine dayanma ve ondan yardım alma
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Dayanmanın yanında yardım isteme, tek seçeneğe bağlanma veya işi ona yöneltme kapsamlarına uzanır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dalda da bir kişi bir iş için başka bir kişiye dayanır.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal bir güvenip dayanma eylemi veya tutumudur; komşu dal bunu kişinin güçsüzlüğü ve işini aksatmasıyla belirlenen kalıcı bir nitelik olarak sunar.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Belirli bir işte başkasına dayanma ve güvenme tutumunu anlatır; kalıcı kişilik kusuru şart değildir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Başkasına dayanması yüzünden kendi işini yürütemeyen güçsüz ve etkisiz kişi niteliğini anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dalda başkasına dayanma ilişkisi bulunur.

branches.source_phrase_ar: التوكل منه وهو إظهار العجز في الأمر والاعتماد على غيرك (maqayis)؛ وكلت بالله وتوكلت على الله (ayn)؛ التوكل إظهار العجز والاعتماد على غيرك (sihah)؛ قد اتكل فلان عليك (tahdhib)؛ توكلت عليه بمعنى اعتمدته (mufradat)

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, kişinin kendi yetersizliğini kabul edip işinde başkasına dayanması ve ona güvenmesi üzerinde birleşir; kullanım hem Tanrı'ya hem de insanlara yöneltilebilir.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه التوكل على الله والاتكال على فلان واعتماد المرء غيره في أمره

concept_gloss.applicability: Kişinin güçsüzlüğünü, başkasına bağımlılığını ve kendi işini yürütememesini birlikte anlatan genel karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Güçsüzlük, bağımlılık ve işin aksaması yönlerinin tümünü korur.

concept_gloss.text: güçsüzlüğü yüzünden işini başkasına bırakıp aksatan kişi

concept_map.definition: Güçsüz ve etkisiz olduğu için kendi işini başkasına bırakan, sürekli ona dayanan ve bunun sonucunda işini gereğince yürütemeyen kişidir.

facets.statement: Kişi güçsüzdür, etkili davranamaz ve kendi işini başkasına bırakır.
Başkasına sürekli dayanması kendi işinin aksamasına veya boşa çıkmasına yol açar.
Bazı kullanımlarda kişinin ağır ve çeviklikten uzak oluşu da bu niteliğin görünümü sayılır.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kişinin güçsüzlüğü ve kendi sorumluluğunu sürekli başkasına bırakması öne çıktığında kullanılır.

error_profile.loses: Bu bağımlılığın işi aksatması sonucunu açıkça belirtmez.
error_profile.preserves: Güçsüzlük ve işi başkasına bırakma yönlerini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kişinin başkasına bağımlılığı yüzünden kendi işinin boşa çıkması veya aksaması vurgulandığında kullanılır.

error_profile.loses: Kişinin genel güçsüzlük ve etkisizlik niteliğini açıkça söylemez.
error_profile.preserves: Başkalarına bağımlılık ile işin aksaması arasındaki ilişkiyi korur.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal geçici olarak yardım alan kişiyi değil, güçsüzlüğü ve başkasına bağımlılığı kendi işini yürütmesini engelleyen kişiyi anlatır.
identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, güçsüz ve etkisiz olduğu için kendi işini başkasına bırakan, ona dayanan ve bu yüzden işini aksatan kişiyi tanımlar. Verilen dal çerçevesi kişi niteliğini, bağımlılık ilişkisini ve işin yürümemesi sonucunu doğru biçimde bir arada tutar.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: güçsüz, etkisiz ve işini başkasına bırakan kişi
işini insanlara bırakıp başkasına dayanan kişi
başkasına dayanıp işini aksatan veya çevik olmayan kişi

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, kişi adları ve çekimli bir eylem kullanımından çıkan ortak niteliği korur; bu biçimlerden bağımsız bir yalın kök anlamı varsaymaz.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar güçsüzlük, bağımlılık, ihmal ve kişi niteliği bakımından değerlendirildi; seçilen üç komşu, dalın başkasına dayanarak işi aksatma koşulunu en açık biçimde sınırlar.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal güçsüzlüğü başkasına bağımlılık ve kendi işini yürütememe ile sınırlar; komşu dal ise daha genel bir güçsüzlük ya da çaresizlik niteliğidir.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Güçsüz kişinin işini başkasına bırakıp ona dayanması ve bu yüzden işini aksatması gerekir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Güçsüzlük veya çaresizlik, başkasına dayanma ve işi aksatma bulunmadan da anlatılabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal kişideki güçsüzlük ve yetersizlik niteliğini paylaşır.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal ihmalin nedenini güçsüzlük ve başkasına bağımlılık olarak belirler; komşu dal işi yürütmeme durumunu daha geniş davranış ve nedenlerle kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: İşin aksaması, güçsüz kişinin sorumluluğu başkasına bırakıp ona dayanmasından doğar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: İşi ihmal etme tembellik, oyalanma, görmezden gelme veya çok yatma gibi başka nedenlere dayanabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da kişinin kendi işini gereğince yürütmemesi alanında buluşur.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal bağımlılığı olumsuz bir kişi niteliği ve başarısızlık sonucu olarak verir; komşu dal ise yalnızca güvenip dayanma eylemini anlatabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Başkasına dayanmayı kişiyi tanımlayan güçsüzlük ve işini aksatma niteliğiyle birleştirir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Belirli bir işte başkasına güvenip dayanmayı anlatır; kişinin güçsüz bir karakter olması veya işi aksatması gerekmez.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dalın ortak öğesi kişinin kendi işi için başkasına dayanmasıdır.

branches.source_phrase_ar: الوَكَلَة والوَكَل الرجل الضعيف (maqayis)؛ رجل وكل ووكلة وهو المواكل يتكل على غيره فيضيع أمره (ayn)؛ رجل وكل ووكلة وتكلة أي عاجز يكل أمره إلى غيره (sihah)؛ رجل وكل إذا كان ضعيفا ليس بنافذ (tahdhib)؛ رجل وكلة تكلة إذا اعتمد غيره في أمره (mufradat)

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak tanımı, güçsüz ve etkisiz kişinin kendi işini başkasına bırakıp ona dayanmasıdır; işin aksaması bu bağımlılığın sonucu, çevik olmama ise daha dar bir görünümüdür.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه الرجل الوَكَل والوُكَلَة والتُّكَلَة والمواكل إذا كان ضعيفا يعتمد على غيره ويضيع أمره
branches.what_is_not_ar: ليس هو الوكيل القائم بالأمر ولا الفرس الواكل

concept_gloss.applicability: İki kişinin veya bir topluluğun üyelerinin kendi yükümlülükleri bakımından karşılıklı biçimde ötekine dayandığı kullanımlara uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Karşılıklı dayanma ilişkisini ve iki taraflı katılımı bütünüyle korur.

concept_gloss.text: tarafların işte karşılıklı olarak birbirine dayanması

concept_map.definition: İki kişinin ya da bir topluluktaki kişilerin her birinin kendi payına düşen işte karşısındakine dayanması ve karşı tarafın da aynı biçimde ona dayanmasıdır.

facets.statement: Dayanma tek yönlü değildir; ilişkinin iki tarafı da işi bakımından ötekine dayanır.
Aynı karşılıklı ilişki, iki kişiyle sınırlı kalmayıp bir topluluğun bütün üyeleri arasında gerçekleşebilir.

contextual_glosses.applicability: İki tarafın da kendi payına düşen işi ötekinin üstleneceğini düşünerek ona dayandığı bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.loses: İlişkinin daha geniş bir topluluğun bütün üyelerini kapsayabilmesini dışarıda bırakır.
error_profile.preserves: İki tarafın da işi bakımından ötekine dayanması yönünü korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Karşılıklı dayanmanın iki kişiden daha geniş bir topluluk içinde gerçekleştiği bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.loses: İki kişi arasındaki daha dar kullanımı doğrudan karşılamaz.
error_profile.preserves: Topluluğun üyeleri arasındaki karşılıklı dayanma yönünü korur.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Karşılıklılık zorunludur; işin aksaması olası bir bağlam sonucu olabilir, fakat bu dalın kaynakça doğrulanmış kurucu anlamı değildir.
identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, iki kişinin veya bir topluluğun her üyesinin karşılıklı biçimde ötekine dayanmasını açıkça bildirir. Ancak işin bu yüzden boşa çıkacağını kaynak ifadesinin kurucu bir parçası olarak söylemez; bu nedenle dal korunmuş, tanım yalnızca karşılıklı dayanma ilişkisine göre yeniden çerçevelenmiştir.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: birine dayanmak, onun da sana dayanması

lexicalization_scope.note: Anlam yalnızca karşılıklılık bildiren türemiş kullanımlara bağlıdır; yalın bir kök anlamı olarak veya tek yönlü dayanma için genellenmez.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar karşılıklılık, tek yönlü bağımlılık, ihmal ve bağlam özgüllüğü bakımından değerlendirildi; yayımlanan ilişkiler zorunlu karşılıklılık sınırını en iyi gösterenlerdir.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal karşılıklı dayanmanın genel ilişki yapısını verir; komşu dal aynı yapıyı savaş ortamına ve tarafların birbirine sığınmasına özgüler.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Karşılıklı dayanmayı genel olarak iki kişi veya bir topluluk arasında anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Karşılıklı dayanmayı savaş ortamında birbirine sığınma ve birbirini dayanak edinme biçimiyle sınırlar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dalda topluluktaki kişiler karşılıklı olarak birbirine dayanır.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dalın ayırıcı yönü karşılıklılıktır; komşu dalın ayırıcı yönü ise bir kişinin güçsüzlüğü ve kendi işini yürütememesidir.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: İlişkinin bütün taraflarının karşılıklı biçimde birbirine dayanmasını zorunlu kılar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Tek bir güçsüz kişinin başkasına dayanarak kendi işini aksatmasını anlatır; karşılıklılık gerekmez.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dalda da kişi kendi işi bakımından başkasına dayanır.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal iki ya da daha çok taraf arasında karşılıklı bağımlılık kurar; komşu dalda güvenip dayanma tek yönlü olabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Her iki tarafın da ötekine dayanmasını gerektirir ve güven ilişkisinin yönünü karşılıklı kılar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Bir kişinin başka birine veya Tanrı'ya tek yönlü güvenip dayanmasını anlatabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dalda bir iş için başka bir varlığa dayanma bulunur.

branches.source_phrase_ar: واكلت الرجل إذا اتكلت عليه واتكل عليك (maqayis)؛ واكلت فلانا مواكلة إذا اتكلت عليه واتكل هو عليك (sihah)؛ تواكل القوم إذا اتكل كل على الآخر (mufradat)

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, iki tarafın da birbirine dayandığı karşılıklı ilişki üzerinde birleşir ve bu ilişkiyi bir topluluğun her üyesinin ötekilere dayanmasına kadar genişletir; işin boşa çıkması ortak iddianın açık bir öğesi değildir.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه واكلت فلانا وتواكل القوم إذا اتكل كل واحد على الآخر فضاع الأمر
branches.what_is_not_ar: ليس هو التوكيل الصحيح ولا التوكل على الله ولا وكال الدابة

concept_gloss.applicability: Hayvanın gecikmesini, hareketini başka hayvana bağlamasını ve kötü yürüyüş görünümünü birlikte kapsayan genel karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Geride kalma, bağımlı hareket ve kötü yürüme yönlerini birlikte korur.

concept_gloss.text: hayvanın geride kalarak veya eşine dayanarak kötü yürümesi

concept_map.definition: Bir hayvanın yürüyüşte sürekli geride kalması, ancak başka bir hayvan hareket edince yürümesi veya koşuda eşine dayanmasıdır; bazı kullanımlarda daha genel biçimde kötü yürümesini de anlatır.

facets.statement: Hayvan öteki hayvanların gerisinde kalır veya geride kalmaya eğilim gösterir.
Hayvan kendi başına ilerlemek yerine başka hayvanın yürüyüşüne ya da koşuda eşine dayanır.
Bir kullanım, bu bağımlı veya gecikmeli hareketi daha genel olarak kötü yürüme diye belirtir.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Hayvanın öteki hayvanların arkasında kalması veya geride yürümeyi istemesi öne çıktığında kullanılır.

error_profile.loses: Başka hayvanın hareketine dayanma ve genel kötü yürüme kullanımlarını dışarıda bırakır.
error_profile.preserves: Hayvanın öteki hayvanların gerisinde kalma yönünü korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Atın veya başka bir hayvanın yürümek ya da koşmak için yanındaki hayvanın hareketine dayandığı bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.loses: Sürekli geride kalma ile genel kötü yürüme çeşitlerini dışarıda bırakır.
error_profile.preserves: Hayvanın hareketini eşinin hareketine bağlama yönünü korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kaynağın hayvanın hareket kusurunu daha genel bir kötü yürüyüş olarak verdiği dar kullanımda uygundur.

error_profile.loses: Geride kalma ve başka hayvana dayanma biçimlerini açıkça belirtmez.
error_profile.preserves: Hayvanın hareketindeki bozukluk ve yetersizlik yönünü korur.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal genel yavaşlığı değil, hayvanın geride kalma, kötü yürüme veya hareketini başka hayvanın hareketine bağlama biçimlerini kapsar.
identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi hayvanın sürekli geride kalması veya geride kalmayı istemesi, ancak başka hayvanın yürüyüşüyle yürümesi, koşuda eşine dayanması ya da kötü yürümesi gibi ilişkili hareket bozukluklarını bir araya getirir. Verilen çerçeve, gecikme ve başka hayvana bağımlı hareket çekirdeğini bu çeşitleri silmeden korur.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: hayvanın geride kalması ya da ancak öteki hayvanlarla yürümesi
koşuda eşine dayanıp dürtülmeye ihtiyaç duyan at

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, hayvanla kurulan kalıpları ve kötü yürümeyi bildiren çekimli kullanımı ayrı yüzler olarak korur; hiçbirini sınırsız bir yalın kök anlamına dönüştürmez.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar hız, adım düzeni, hareket kalitesi ve başka hayvana bağımlılık bakımından değerlendirildi; seçilen üç karşılaştırma sıradan yavaşlık ile bu dalın bağımlı hareket yapısını ayırır.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalın ayırıcı yönü geride kalma ve eşe bağımlı harekettir; komşu dal ise hızdan çok kısa ve sık adımlı yürüyüş biçimini belirler.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Hayvanın geride kalmasını, başka hayvanın hareketine dayanmasını veya genel olarak kötü yürümesini içerir.
neighbor_distinctions.gloss: kısa ve sık adımlarla yavaş yürüme
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Yavaşlığı, adımların kısa ve birbirine yakın olması biçiminde özel bir yürüyüş düzeniyle tanımlar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal hayvanın yavaş veya yetersiz görünen yürüyüşünü anlatır.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal gecikme ve eşe dayanma eksenindedir; komşu dal koşunun gevşekliği ile hareketin parça parça sürmesini merkez alır.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Hareket kusurunu geride kalma veya başka hayvanın hareketine dayanma ilişkisiyle belirler.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Atın koşusunun gevşemesi ve hareketin parça parça, düşer gibi sürmesi yönünü içerir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da atın veya başka bir hayvanın bozuk ve yetersiz hareketini betimler.

branches.source_phrase_ar: الوكال في الدابة أن يتأخر أبدا خلف الدواب (maqayis)؛ الوكال في الدابة أن تحب التأخر خلف الدواب (ayn)؛ فرس واكل يتكل على صاحبه في العدو (sihah)؛ واكلت الدابة وكالا إذا أساءت السير (tahdhib)؛ الوكال في الدابة أن لا يمشي إلا بمشي غيره (mufradat)

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar hayvanın geride kalması, başka hayvanın hareketine veya koşuda eşine dayanması ve kötü yürümesi gibi birbirine bağlı hareket kusurlarını bildirir; bunlar yalnızca sıradan hız düşüklüğüne indirgenmez.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه الوكال في الدابة وواكلت الدابة والفرس الواكل والمواكل من الخيل إذا أبطأ أو أساء السير واتكل على صاحبه
branches.what_is_not_ar: ليس هو ضعف الإنسان ولا المواكلة بين الناس ولا الوكيل

concept_gloss.applicability: Bir işi devralan kişinin onu yürütme, koruma, yeterli olma ve güvence sağlama işlevlerini birlikte anlatan genel karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: İşi üstlenme, yürütme, koruma, yeterlilik ve güvence yönlerini birlikte korur.

concept_gloss.text: kendisine bırakılan işi üstlenip koruyan yeterli görevli

concept_map.definition: Kendisine bırakılan işi üstlenip yürüten, işi koruyan, onun için yeterli olan ve gerektiğinde güvence veren görevli kişidir.

facets.statement: Kişi, kendisine bırakılan işi üstlenir ve onun yürütülmesinden sorumlu olur.
Görevli, üstlendiği iş için yeterlilik, koruma ve güvence sağlama işlevlerini taşır.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kendisine bırakılan işi devralma ve onun yürütülmesinden sorumlu olma yönü öne çıktığında kullanılır.

error_profile.loses: Koruma, yeterli olma ve güvence verme işlevlerini açıkça belirtmez.
error_profile.preserves: İşi üstlenme ve yürütme sorumluluğunu korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Görevlinin üstlendiği iş için koruma, yeterlilik ve güvence sağlaması vurgulandığında kullanılır.

error_profile.loses: İşin önceden bu kişiye bırakılmış olması ilişkisini açıkça belirtmez.
error_profile.preserves: Koruma, yeterlilik ve güvence sağlama işlevlerini korur.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, kendisine bırakılan işi yeterlilik, koruma ve güvenceyle yürüten görevliye aittir; tekil deve sahibi kullanımı bu çekirdeği genişletmez.
identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, kendisine iş bırakıldığı için onu üstlenen, yeterli olan, koruyan ve güvence veren görevliyi anlatır. Geçici dal çerçevesindeki deve sahibi anlamı yetkili branch claim içinde bulunmadığından tanımın kurucu parçası yapılmamış, yalnızca ilgili söz biriminin ayrı karşılığında korunmuştur.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: işi üstlenen, koruyan, yeterli olan ve güvence veren görevli

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, işi üstlenme eylemi ile görevliyi bildiren biçimleri ayırır; ayrı ve tekil deve sahibi karşılığını dalın genel anlamına katmaz.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar görevi üstlenme, koruma, yeterlilik ve temsil sınırları bakımından değerlendirildi; seçilen üç komşu görevlinin sorumluluğunu genel koruma ve yeterlilikten ayırır.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal korumayı devredilmiş işi üstlenme, yeterlilik ve güvenceyle birleştirir; komşu dal ise gözetme ve bakım işlevini daha geniş, bağımsız bir çekirdek olarak taşır.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Kişinin kendisine bırakılan işi yürütmesini, iş için yeterli olmasını ve güvence vermesini içerir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Bir şeyi gözetme, sürekli koruma, bakımını izleme ve emanet olarak saklama alanını daha geniş biçimde kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dalda bir kişi kendisine bırakılan şeyi korur ve onunla ilgilenir.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal devralanın görev ve yeterlilik niteliğine, komşu dal ise bu görevi kuran devretme ve yetkilendirme işlemine odaklanır.
neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Görevi alan kişinin işi yeterince yürütme, koruma ve güvence sağlama niteliğini anlatır.

text.arabic_uthmani: رَّبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِكُمْ ۖ إِن يَشَأْ يَرْحَمْكُمْ أَوْ إِن يَشَأْ يُعَذِّبْكُمْ ۚ وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَٰكَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَكِيلًۭا

baseline.text: Rabbiniz sizi en iyi bilir. Dilerse size merhamet eder, dilerse size azap eder. Seni onların üzerine bir vekil olarak göndermedik.

findings.text: İnsanların içini ve sonucunu bilme yetkisinin Allah'a ait olması, peygamberin görevini sonuçlara sahip olmadan bildirmekle sınırlar; hitap sorumluluğu zorlayıcı vesayet değildir.

activation_trace.role: Lordship contributes ownership and sovereignty, making the Lord the governing subject of both alternatives.
Knowledge as disclosure to the knower grounds the outcomes in an access to persons that hearers do not possess.
The repeated will branch supplies the operative hinge that keeps mercy and punishment under one agent's volition.

changed_reading.after: The ayah relocates judgment into a Lord whose intimate knowledge governs either outcome, withholding any basis for hearers to pre-classify themselves or others.
changed_reading.before: The ayah merely lists two things God might do to people.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: رَبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِكُمْ ... إِن يَشَأْ ... إِن يَشَأْ
baseline_models.mechanism: Lordship and superior knowledge precede two parallel will-conditionals, so both possible outcomes remain acts of informed divine governance rather than conclusions available to the audience.

activation_trace.role: The messenger-and-message branch defines an office of carrying communicated content.
Delegation of an affair supplies the exact authority relation that the negation refuses.
Custodial sufficiency and preservation sharpen what the messenger is not charged to provide over them.

changed_reading.after: The messenger carries the message but is neither the audience's delegated manager nor the custodian who must secure its response or destiny.
changed_reading.before: Being sent makes the messenger responsible for securing the audience's final condition.

baseline_models.mechanism: The sending construction assigns transmission, while the explicit negation of agency blocks any transfer of the people's affairs, preservation, or outcome-management to the messenger.

activation_trace.role: Repair, nurture, and completion make lordship an active process of bringing dependents through changing conditions.
Tenderness and beneficence supply the positive mode of divine handling.
Pain and punishment supply the severe consequential mode paired with mercy.

changed_reading.after: Mercy and painful consequence are two still-open divine treatments; the ayah names their range while refusing to assign either outcome through the messenger.
changed_reading.before: Mercy is a favorable label and punishment an unfavorable label already attachable to groups.

baseline_models.mechanism: Tender beneficence and painful consequence form a real pair, but the repeated conditional prevents either pole from becoming the messenger's verdict; both remain possible modes of the Lord's handling.

activation_trace.role: Custodial sufficiency names the authority denied to the messenger and therefore limits the scope of his address.
The good opposed to the ugly supplies the required quality of speech under conflict.
Corrupting relations by incitement supplies the social mechanism that careful speech is meant to interrupt.
The connection standing between parties supplies the relational field damaged by incitement and protected by better speech.

changed_reading.after: The line disciplines address: speak in the best way, resist relational incitement, and leave the audience's merciful or punitive outcome with the Lord who knows them.
changed_reading.before: The mercy-or-punishment line authorizes blunt classification of the people being addressed.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately preceding command answers interpersonal provocation with the best speech because hostile speech tears relations apart; the following denial of custodianship prevents that speech duty from becoming a license to sentence its recipients.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies best speech, relational incitement, and a denied custodial office; I infer that the denial restrains verdict-like speech, while a live alternative is that it only consoles the messenger about failed persuasion.
structural_cues: 17:53 commands speech before 17:54 assigns knowledge and outcomes to the Lord.
The second-person plural audience of 17:54 follows a command concerning what the servants should say to one another.

activation_trace.role: A screening barrier supplies a hidden interface between recitation and its resistant hearers.
Protective covering contributes an inward occlusion placed over the hearts.
Weight in the ear supplies a bodily image for impeded reception.
The contextual 'We know best' assigns access to the concealed manner of listening before the focus repeats that epistemic priority.
Hearing as understanding and compliance distinguishes acoustic exposure from receptive uptake.
Secret counsel contributes an interior social layer unavailable from public speech alone.
The denied custodial branch prevents responsibility for hidden uptake from being assigned to the messenger.

changed_reading.after: The knowledge claim targets a concrete epistemic asymmetry: God accesses the layered, hidden process of reception, while the messenger encounters only its outward effects and cannot own its outcome.
changed_reading.before: God knows the audience better only in a general omniscience formula.

context_deltas.mechanism: Layered barriers, coverings, auditory weight, modes of listening, and secret counsel make reception partly inaccessible; the repeated knowledge claim then assigns interior access to God and explains why the messenger cannot be custodian of the hearers' response.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies concealed and impaired reception plus an exact knowledge reprise; I infer that inaccessible uptake is why final custody cannot rest with the messenger, though the barriers could alternatively describe culpability without explaining the office boundary.
structural_cues: 17:45-48 moves from a barrier and covered hearts to hidden listening, covert counsel, misleading comparisons, and inability to find a path.
17:47's 'We know best' is resumed by 17:54's 'your Lord knows best.'

activation_trace.role: Turning something from state to state supplies the varied presentation repeatedly offered to the audience.
Increase and growth mark the counter-result produced in the recipients.
Recoil and distancing name the adverse uptake that grows despite repeated presentation.
Putting fear into others supplies the warning action whose intended caution is not guaranteed.
A second increase construction links the later reversal to the earlier growth of aversion.
Exceeding the limit in rebellion supplies the paradoxical result of warning in resistant hearers.
Message-bearing defines successful commission independently of the audience's reaction.
The denied custodial role blocks the messenger from being measured as controller of the reaction.

changed_reading.after: Delivery can expose and even intensify an existing resistant trajectory; the messenger is responsible for the sending role, not for engineering a merciful response.
changed_reading.before: A properly delivered message should mechanically move its hearers toward mercy, so resistance suggests a failure of delivery.

context_deltas.mechanism: Varied presentation and warning can produce the reverse of their communicative aim, increasing aversion or transgression; the non-custodial clause separates faithful sending from control of this nonlinear uptake.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two explicit reception reversals and the office contrast; I infer that the contrast protects the sending role from outcome-control, while an alternative is that the repeated reversals only characterize persistent opponents.
structural_cues: 17:41 and 17:60 share the form 'it does not increase them except,' first with aversion and then with great transgression.
The focus clause distinguishes being sent from being placed over the recipients.

activation_trace.role: Fragmentation and debris supply the apparent material endpoint disputed by the resurrection question.
Creative origination supplies the act whose renewal the speakers consider impossible.
Return after departure supplies the temporal reversal asked about by the audience.
Origination and beginning identify the agent capable of reversing fragmentation.
A summons by speech supplies the initiating act of the future transition.
Answering speech supplies the recipients' compelled transition from inert remains to responsive subjects.
Sovereign lordship makes the same agent governor of the reconstituted subjects' subsequent outcome.

changed_reading.after: The alternatives remain open across the coming reconstitution: the One who can call fragmented people back also governs what follows, while the messenger neither restores nor assigns them.
changed_reading.before: Mercy and punishment in 17:54 concern only the audience's present treatment.

context_deltas.mechanism: The sequence moves fragmented remains through imaginable hard forms to originating, returning, calling, and answering; this gives the mercy-punishment alternative a horizon of divine reconstitution rather than an immediate social verdict.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a material and temporal restoration sequence followed by mercy or punishment; I infer that restoration opens the arena for those outcomes, while the alternatives may also include present-world mercy and punishment.
structural_cues: 17:50 tests stone and iron as imagined escape-forms.
17:52 places the call-and-response on a future day immediately before the speech command and focus ayah.

activation_trace.role: Selection of a chosen portion supplies the disputed claim of preferential allocation.
Saying or ascribing what was not so identifies the allocation claim as speech-generated rather than knowledge-grounded.
The repeated Lord title restores allocation to the sovereign owner.
The exact knowledge reprise grounds differential treatment in divine access to those treated.
Degree and excellence supply a real hierarchy that contrasts with the fabricated preference in 17:40.
Partition into portions supplies the differentiated distribution among prophets.
The prophet who conveys from God places the messenger himself within, rather than above, the allocated order.
Denied delegation prevents prophetic rank from becoming delegated ownership of other persons' destinies.

changed_reading.after: The ayah also bars status entitlement: neither communities nor messengers may convert claimed privilege into control of mercy, punishment, or rank; the knowledgeable Lord apportions them.
changed_reading.before: The ayah only contrasts God's knowledge with ordinary ignorance.

context_deltas.mechanism: A false human claim about the Lord's preferential selection is answered later by an actual, differentiated divine favor among prophets; the focus knowledge formula makes allocation the Lord's informed act rather than a status people may claim or distribute.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies fabricated preference, exact knowledge language, and actual differentiated favor; I infer that 17:54 corrects entitlement and locates allocation with the Lord, while 17:55 may concern prophetic gifts rather than the mercy-punishment allocation itself.
structural_cues: 17:40 asks whether 'your Lord selected you,' while 17:55 repeats 'your Lord knows best' and states that some prophets were favored over others.
The focus lies between the false allocation claim and the explicit divine allocation.

activation_trace.role: Possession and power of disposal supply precisely the control denied to invoked intermediaries.
Lifting a covering supplies the concrete action of removing affliction that intermediaries cannot perform.
Harm and loss name the adverse condition whose removal is outside their possession.
Transfer from one state to another supplies the alternative form of control also denied.
Seeking supplies the intermediaries' dependent movement toward a means rather than sovereign command.
The heart's expectation of what is hoped for makes mercy an awaited gift, not a possession.
Tender beneficence is the same mercy hoped for by the context's apparently elevated subjects.
Anticipatory fear makes punishment a live possibility for the same subjects who hope for mercy.
Painful punishment supplies the feared outcome repeated from the focus ayah.
The denied custodian joins the later denial of intermediary control into one distribution of agency.

changed_reading.after: Even elevated beings stand together between hope and fear and cannot transfer harm; mercy and punishment are a shared open horizon under God alone, consistent with the messenger's non-custodial office.
changed_reading.before: Mercy names one settled class, punishment another, and powerful intermediaries may help determine placement.

context_deltas.mechanism: Those invoked besides God cannot own the removal or transfer of harm and themselves seek nearness while hoping for mercy and fearing punishment; this turns the focus alternatives from labels assigned to separate camps into a shared horizon controlled by no intermediary.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies inability to own harm's removal plus simultaneous hope and fear; I infer that 17:54 reserves outcome-control to God rather than sorting fixed camps, while the referents in 17:57 may differ from the direct audience of 17:54.
structural_cues: 17:57's branchless و س ل occurrence presents a sought means of approach but cannot itself serve as a branch citation.
Mercy and punishment recur together in 17:57, where hope and fear belong to the same grammatical subjects.

activation_trace.role: Painful punishment supplies the severe outcome stated as part of the written order.
Binding inscription that establishes a judgment or measure contributes the register of divine governance.
An ordered written line makes the consequence inspectably recorded rather than delegated to a messenger.
A barrier between an agent and what is sought supplies divine control over whether signs are sent.
Sending and release supply the delivery action applied to signs without implying custody of their recipients.
Manifest signs supply evidentiary disclosure rather than coercive conversion.
Inducing fear defines the signs' stated warning function.
The repeated Lord title identifies the sovereign agent of the encompassing that follows.
Complete encompassing in knowledge and securing supplies the total relation to people denied to the messenger.
Vision in sleep supplies disclosed material whose reception becomes a test rather than an enforced conclusion.
Testing a person as metal is tested supplies an exposure mechanism whose result emerges from the subject.
Denied custodial sufficiency marks the messenger's narrower relation inside the divinely encompassed field.

changed_reading.after: It is a positive allocation of roles: the Lord encompasses, records, tests, and governs outcomes; the messenger and signs disclose and warn within that field without enforcing response.
changed_reading.before: Not being a custodian is merely a negative limitation on the messenger.

context_deltas.mechanism: Written consequence, selectively sent signs, warning, trial, and the Lord's encompassing of people divide agency sharply: divine governance encloses and records the field, whereas what is sent discloses and warns within it without taking custody of recipients.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies decree, controlled sending, warning, testing, and divine encompassing; I infer a division between God's total governance and the messenger's revelatory function, while 'encompassed' could denote knowledge or threatened defeat rather than custodial preservation.
structural_cues: 17:58 places punishment in a written register; 17:59 defines sent signs as warning; 17:60 says the Lord encompasses the people and makes a vision a trial.
The repeated sending root in 17:59 extends the focus ayah's contrast between transmission and custodianship.

remaining_uncertainties: Whether the plural 'you' is scoped primarily to the immediate resistant audience, human beings generally, or shifting interlocutors in the sequence.
Whether mercy and punishment are chiefly present treatments, post-reconstitution outcomes, or intentionally span both horizons.
Whether divine encompassing in 17:60 should sharpen knowledge, custody, threatened defeat, or more than one of these.
The womb-weaning and will-thing activations are packet-anchored but remain deliberately form-distant and should not control a conservative synthesis.
strongest_changes: The immediate speech command turns the ayah into a restraint on verdict-like address: better speech remains obligatory while outcomes remain divine.
Hidden and nonlinear reception explain the messenger's non-custodial office: he carries disclosure but cannot own interior uptake or reverse reactions.
The exact 17:55 knowledge reprise relocates preference and rank from human entitlement to informed divine allocation.
The 17:56-57 sequence makes mercy and punishment a simultaneous horizon of hope and fear under God alone, not two camps controlled by intermediaries.
The 17:58-60 sequence positively divides roles: divine encompassing, decree, and testing contrast with sent warning that does not enforce response.
summary.what_was_special: The focus ayah acts as a hinge. It converts the preceding ethics and opacity of reception into an office boundary, then the following exact knowledge reprise, intermediary incapacity, warning signs, and divine encompassing unpack why that boundary matters.

activation_trace.role: Gradual nurture and completion supply a developmental frame for the Lord's handling of persons.
The womb as a house and vessel of growth supplies an enclosing image for mercy.
Restraint, prevention, and weaning supply a separating discipline that can be set against merciful enclosure.
Custodial care names the proxy role explicitly denied to the messenger.

changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the Lord alone governs a developmental passage between protective enclosure and painful separation or restraint; the messenger is not a surrogate custodian of that passage.
changed_reading.before: Mercy and punishment are only opposed legal outcomes.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates bodily and developmental branches rather than the ordinary abstract senses. It remains anchored in the focus roots for lordly nurture, womb-mercy, restraining or weaning, and custody. Downstream prose should present it as a material analogy for the relation among the clauses, not as a claim that the verbal forms lexically mean womb or weaning here.

activation_trace.role: The knowable and reportable thing supplies the populated field whose praise exceeds human comprehension.
Failure to understand supplies the human epistemic limit against which divine willing is heard.
Will related to bringing about or reaching a thing supplies an actualizing resonance in both conditionals.
Superior knowledge links the Lord's willing to access beyond the audience's limited comprehension.

changed_reading.after: As a contained lexical resonance, divine willing brings either outcome into the field of actual things while human beings remain unable to comprehend even the wider field already praising.
changed_reading.before: The two conditionals merely select between two already static options.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it lets a contextual noun and the focus verbs activate two branches of the same root across distinct forms. It remains anchored in the packet's shared ش ي ء inventory and the repeated conditionals. Downstream prose should call it lexical resonance, not derive a doctrine of creation from the syntax or erase the ordinary sense of willing.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Unknown judgment limits the messenger's custodial reach.** `ع ل م:B001` clear knowledge, `ر ح م:B001` mercy, `ع ذ ب:B003/B005` withholding and punishment, `ر س ل:B001/B004` sending with deliberate pace, and `و ك ل:B001/B006` delegated guardianship. Mercy/punishment remain under divine knowing, then agency over hearers is explicitly not delegated. I infer epistemic asymmetry blocks coercive custody. The messenger's task reads as transmission without ownership of outcomes.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 17:96's sufficient witness “between me and you” gives the positive limit of agency: the messenger need not control judgment because comprehensive witnessing already occupies the interval.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Speech-guidance without custodial takeover.** Lexical evidence: `ر ح م B001` (mercy and tenderness) in `يَرْحَمْكُمْ`, `ع ذ ب B005` (torment and punishment) in `يُعَذِّبْكُمْ`, and `و ك ل B006` (one who undertakes, suffices, and guards) in negated `وَكِيلًا`. Structural cue: 17:53 commands the messenger to regulate what servants say, but this ayah reserves knowledge and outcome to the Lord; 17:55 differentiates prophets, and 17:56 denies other figures power to remove harm. Assigned role: the messenger transmits an intervention in speech, while negated guardianship blocks control of persons and outcomes. Abductive move: the role boundary is supplied; I infer that exhortation works through address rather than forced management. Reading change: the ayah distinguishes communicative responsibility from sovereign custody, preserving mercy and punishment as divine decisions.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 17:56 and 17:59 sharpened the role boundary from two sides: neither invoked figures nor visible signs compel outcomes, so messengerhood remains warning and address rather than sovereign management.

words.gloss_range: address-bound Lord title grounding knowledge, mercy, and punishment
words.prose: {{ar:رَّبُّكُمْ}} ({{tr:rabbukum}}) begins as the subject of a nominal claim, so the ayah opens with a standing Lord-relation before any outcome verb appears. The suffix makes that lordship directly address-bound, and the title carries authority together with nurture, correction, and completion; mercy and punishment are therefore framed as acts inside one governing relation, not unrelated options. The reprise of the {{tr:rabbukum aʿlamu}} frame from 17:25 broadens the earlier inner-state knowledge into knowledge of the addressees themselves, while the compressed doubled sound gives the opening title weight.
words.root_gloss_range: lordship range including ownership, nurture, correction, and completion; the local title binds that range to the addressees

topics.headline: address-bound opening Lord-title
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the first word binds the addressees to a standing Lord-relation before the ayah names mercy or punishment.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence make the word the nominative subject of the opening nominal sentence and attach the second-person plural suffix to it.

topics.headline: nurturing authority range
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the title combines ownership, nurture, correction, and completion, so the later alternatives remain acts of one Lord rather than competing divine moods.
topics.reason: The root-family evidence supports lord, owner, nurturer, reformer, and completer, while local grammar selects the concrete title rather than activating every root branch equally.

topics.headline: surah refrain and compressed opening sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears this opening as a Surah 17 reprise whose sound and wording concentrate authority before the conditionals begin.
topics.reason: The phrase recurs at 17:25, and contextual evidence links it to the surah-local mercy thread; the phonetic row supplies a local acoustic payoff.

words.gloss_range: elative predicate of superior divine knowledge concerning the addressees
words.prose: {{ar:أَعْلَمُ}} ({{tr:aʿlamu}}) is the elative predicate of the opening title: the claim is that the Lord is more knowing or most knowing concerning the addressees. Because no explicit comparator follows, the form keeps both surpassing and superlative force, grounding the coming mercy-or-punishment alternatives in superior knowledge rather than arbitrary reaction. The word is an adjective here, not a Form IV verb of informing, and its sharp onset marks the turn from title to predicate; same-surah echoes at 17:25 and 17:55 make this knowledge claim a local refrain.
words.root_gloss_range: knowledge as certain cognition and evaluative competence; teaching or informing branches are not the local form

topics.headline: elative predicate of divine knowledge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah first establishes surpassing divine knowledge before it suspends any outcome under will.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the word as an elative predicate of the opening subject, with no explicit min-comparator.

topics.headline: certain knowledge, not informing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the word names evaluative knowledge of the addressees, not a new act of disclosure to them.
topics.reason: V4 supports knowledge, teaching, and informing branches, but QAC morphology selects a nominative elative adjective rather than the homographic Form IV verb.

topics.headline: Surah 17 knowledge refrain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the word as part of a Surah 17 knowledge refrain that moves from inner states at 17:25 to the broader addressee-domain here and forward to 17:55.
topics.reason: Contextual evidence links this elative with the same-surah knowledge pattern and with the immediate authority-knowledge pairing.

topics.headline: audible predicate onset
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the title-to-predicate turn because the hamza onset gives the elative a distinct entry.
topics.reason: The form has an initial hamza, and the phonetic rows give a local sound payoff that supports the predicate boundary.

words.gloss_range: preposition marking the governed domain of knowledge
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) supplies the governed link that makes the addressees the explicit domain of {{tr:aʿlamu}}. The payoff is not a loose “about” afterthought: {{tr:bikum}} binds knowledge to the persons addressed, broader than the specific inner-state phrase at 17:25. Its tight attachment to the pronoun lets the opening claim land on the audience, and the nasal {{tr:-m}} closes that bound phrase before the conditional section begins.

topics.headline: knowledge-domain marker
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that divine knowledge is explicitly directed concerning the addressees, completing the opening nominal frame.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence make the preposition govern the pronoun as complement of the elative predicate.

topics.headline: bound personal scope
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the preposition makes knowledge personal and attached, not merely content-focused as in 17:25.
topics.reason: The preposition can mark specification and close association; locally it marks the governed knowledge-domain, with attachment as a supporting nuance.

topics.headline: bound phrase closure sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the opening knowledge-domain close before the conditional particle restarts the ayah.
topics.reason: The nasal ending belongs to the bound phrase and supplies a small local closure before the next section.

words.gloss_range: second-person plural bound pronoun as the knowledge-domain and recurring addressee marker
words.prose: {{ar:كُمْ}} ({{tr:kum}}) makes the audience plural and explicit inside the knowledge-domain, then the same suffix returns on the mercy and punishment verbs. The word therefore helps hold one group through knowledge, possible mercy, and possible punishment. Because it is bound rather than independent, the addressees are grammatically carried inside divine relations rather than foregrounded as a separate emphatic subject; boundary evidence links them back to the servants addressed in 17:53.

topics.headline: recurring plural addressees
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks one plural group through the ayah instead of treating mercy and punishment as aimed at different targets.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence mark the same second-person plural suffix in the knowledge phrase and later object suffixes.

topics.headline: bound pronoun as governed domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the addressees as grammatically dependent on the knowledge preposition, not as an independently emphasized pronoun.
topics.reason: The pronoun is governed through the preposition and appears as an attached suffix rather than as an independent pronoun.

topics.headline: servants become direct addressees
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the prior servants of 17:53 carried into direct address under divine knowledge.
topics.reason: Boundary evidence resolves the suffix through the prior ayah, turning a referenced group into direct addressees.

words.gloss_range: first conditional particle making the mercy branch contingent
words.prose: {{ar:إِنْ}} ({{tr:in}}) opens the first conditional gate. It makes the mercy branch genuinely contingent: mercy is named first, but the particle keeps it from becoming automatic. Because the same particle returns before the punishment branch, even with the same nasal onset before each will-verb, the middle of the ayah is heard as matched uncertainty under divine will rather than as a fixed sequence of outcomes.

topics.headline: first conditional gate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that mercy is possible but not grammatically presumed.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the particle as opening the first conditional protasis and governing a jussive structure.

topics.headline: matched conditional architecture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears two outcomes entering through the same kind of conditional gate.
topics.reason: The first particle prepares the repeated in...aw in architecture, and the sound row supports the repeated onset.

words.gloss_range: jussive will verb opening the mercy condition
words.prose: {{ar:يَشَأْ}} ({{tr:yashaʾ}}) is clipped into the jussive by the conditional particle, so the mercy branch is grammatically suspended on divine willing. The subject is recoverable from the opening Lord-title but not restated, which makes the clause move quickly from knowledge to will. The root-field links will with realized thingness, yet locally that pressure is narrowed to determining whether mercy becomes actual; the identical verb later keeps will as the constant while outcomes vary.
words.root_gloss_range: divine willing as determining volition; broader will/thingness pressure is locally narrowed to conditional realization

topics.headline: jussive will protasis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the mercy outcome suspended at the clipped hinge between condition and answer.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the verb as imperfect jussive in the first protasis, with final hamza marking the clipped surface.

topics.headline: direct determining will
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that mercy depends on determining divine will, not on a mood, entitlement, or prophetic agency.
topics.reason: The root supports will and determination, while local grammar selects a direct Form I divine will verb with an implicit subject recoverable from context.

topics.headline: will as shared axis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that mercy and punishment differ as outcomes while divine willing remains the shared axis.
topics.reason: The same will form recurs in both conditional branches, and contextual evidence links the root with both mercy and punishment fields.

words.gloss_range: conditional mercy verb with the addressees as direct object
words.prose: {{ar:يَرْحَمْكُمْ}} ({{tr:yarḥamkum}}) answers the first condition, with the addressees attached as direct object. Mercy is therefore a possible divine action toward them, not a detached quality. Its root-field brings tenderness, beneficence, and protective womb-like care into view, while the jussive frame keeps that care contingent on will. The word also stands before the punishment branch, so mercy receives first mention without becoming a guarantee; within Surah 17 it reworks the mercy wording of 17:8 under the stricter gate of explicit divine will.
words.root_gloss_range: mercy as compassion and active beneficence, with protective womb/kinship imagery as supporting pressure

topics.headline: conditional mercy apodosis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees mercy as the answer to a condition and as an action aimed directly at the addressed group.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the verb as the apodosis of the first condition and the suffix as direct object.

topics.headline: protective mercy field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices mercy as active protective care, not merely non-punishment.
topics.reason: V4 supports compassion, beneficence, and womb/kinship imagery; local Form I verb selects mercy as the action while the image remains supporting pressure.

topics.headline: mercy before punishment in opposition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears mercy first and then hears it held in direct contrast with the heavier punishment branch.
topics.reason: The local conditional pair and contextual evidence make mercy and punishment an opposed field, with shared suffix cadence and contrasting forms.

topics.headline: surah boundary mercy thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the social hostility of 17:53 give way to a possible vertical relation of divine mercy in 17:54.
topics.reason: Same-surah and boundary rows connect this mercy verb with 17:8 and with the transition from interpersonal conflict in 17:53.

words.gloss_range: disjunctive hinge between two complete conditional outcomes
words.prose: {{ar:أَوْ}} ({{tr:aw}}) is the hinge between two complete conditional structures. It does not merely link two verbs; it keeps mercy and punishment as alternatives inside one sovereignty frame, preventing them from collapsing into a sequence. The small standalone particle makes the turn stark, and its sound gives the listener a brief pivot before the second condition starts.

topics.headline: disjunction between complete branches
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees two complete possible outcomes, not one combined predicate.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence place the conjunction between two full conditional clauses.

topics.headline: mercy-punishment antithesis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears mercy and punishment as opposed alternatives held at equal grammatical distance under will.
topics.reason: The conjunction separates the two outcome clauses, and the lexical fields form the local antithesis.

topics.headline: compact turn sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the alternation marked by a brief but weighty particle.
topics.reason: The short standalone form and diphthongal sound supply a local acoustic hinge.

words.gloss_range: repeated conditional particle giving punishment its own full gate
words.prose: The second {{ar:إِنْ}} ({{tr:in}}) is retained, so the punishment branch receives its own full conditional gate instead of borrowing the first one. That repetition keeps punishment suspended just as mercy was suspended. The middle structure becomes balanced: if He wills, mercy; or if He wills, punishment.

topics.headline: retained second conditional gate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees punishment as contingent, not as the inevitable next step after mercy is mentioned.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify a second conditional protasis rather than an elided or reduced continuation.

topics.headline: matched conditional architecture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the repeated particle make divine will constant while the outcomes vary.
topics.reason: The repetition creates matched in yashaʾ branches and prevents the second branch from being subordinate to the first.

words.gloss_range: second jussive will verb opening the punishment condition
words.prose: The second {{ar:يَشَأْ}} ({{tr:yashaʾ}}) repeats the same jussive will verb before the punishment branch. The repetition gives exact parity: the will verb does not intensify when the outcome becomes harsher, and the repeated hamza close makes each protasis stop before its outcome enters. Its root-field again supports determining realization, and wider will-plus-punishment formulas (2:284; 3:129) help show that punishment too is routed through divine sovereignty.
words.root_gloss_range: same determining-will range as word 6, now governing the punishment branch without semantic escalation in the will verb

topics.headline: second jussive will verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the punishment branch governed by the same clipped conditional will as the mercy branch.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence mark the second verb as imperfect jussive under the second conditional particle, with the same recoverable divine subject.

topics.headline: same will before harsher outcome
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the quality of divine willing stays constant even when the following outcome becomes punishment.
topics.reason: The same Form I will verb appears before a Form II punishment verb; local grammar separates the direct will from the heavier outcome form.

topics.headline: sovereignty formula and local echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a broader Quranic sovereignty pattern while also hearing the exact local repetition bind the two branches.
topics.reason: Contextual evidence links will and punishment in formulas such as 2:284 and 3:129, while attachment evidence ties this verb to the earlier identical will verb.

words.gloss_range: conditional Form II punishment verb with the same addressees as direct object
words.prose: {{ar:يُعَذِّبْكُمْ}} ({{tr:yuʿadhdhibkum}}) answers the second condition with the same plural addressees attached as direct object. The word selects punishment or chastisement, but the broader root-field adds narrowed pressure of restraint and reversal from sweetness, making the outcome corrective and severe rather than a generic pain term. Its Form II and doubled sound make it heavier than {{tr:yarḥamkum}}, while cross-references to will-and-punishment formulas (2:284; 3:129) and prophetic non-control (3:128) fit the ayah’s movement into the final role denial.
words.root_gloss_range: punishment/chastisement selected locally, with sweetness and prevention branches only as narrowed root-field pressure

topics.headline: conditional punishment apodosis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees punishment as the answer to the second condition and aimed at the same addressed group.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the verb as the second apodosis and the suffix as direct object.

topics.headline: root-field restraint and reversal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices punishment as chastening restraint and reversal from sweetness, while the local verb still selects punishment.
topics.reason: V4 supports punishment, prevention, and fresh/sweet-water branches; local Form II selects chastisement, so the other branches remain narrowed semantic pressure.

topics.headline: Form II heaviness against mercy
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears and sees punishment made morphologically denser than the lighter mercy verb.
topics.reason: QAC marks the verb as Form II, and the local contrast with Form I mercy supports the heavier morphological and acoustic payoff.

topics.headline: opposition field and prophetic non-control
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the punishment branch as one pole of the mercy-punishment alternative and as part of the same sovereignty logic that excludes prophetic control.
topics.reason: Contextual evidence links mercy and punishment as an opposition field, links will and punishment formulas at 2:284 and 3:129, and notes the prophetic-authority parallel at 3:128.

words.gloss_range: resumptive conjunction pivoting from outcome sovereignty to mission-scope denial
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) pivots out of the completed mercy-or-punishment pair into the final mission-scope clause. It both links the denial to the prior sovereignty logic and resumes with a fresh declaration, so the role boundary is not an unrelated aside. As a clitic fused into {{tr:wa-mā}}, the particle also makes the transition compact and prepares the person shift from third-person “He wills” to first-person divine speech in {{tr:arsalnāka}}.

topics.headline: resumptive pivot to mission scope
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah turn from what God may do to the people to what the Prophet was not commissioned to be.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks a new negated verbal clause after the conditional section, with the conjunction at the boundary.

topics.headline: sovereignty linked to role denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final role denial as the consequence of divine sovereignty, not as a detached administrative note.
topics.reason: The conjunction can coordinate and resume; here both functions are locally coherent because the final clause resolves the previous sovereignty logic.

topics.headline: compact transition into voice shift
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the swift transition into first-person divine delimitation of the Prophet’s role.
topics.reason: The clitic fuses to the negative particle and introduces the clause where divine speech shifts to first-person plural.

words.gloss_range: negative particle denying the sending-as-wakil frame while preserving mission
words.prose: {{ar:مَآ}} ({{tr:mā}}) negates the completed sending-as-{{tr:wakīlā}} frame, not the Prophet’s mission itself. Its scope reaches the {{tr:arsalnāka ʿalayhim wakīlā}} frame: the sending is real, but the capacity of entrusted control over them is refused. The long vowel gives the denial its own recitational beat before the completed sending verb enters.

topics.headline: role negation, not mission negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the Prophet is sent, but not sent as the manager of the people’s outcomes.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the negated verbal clause include the sending verb, authority-domain, and role complement; the negation targets the capacity frame.

topics.headline: independent negative declaration
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final clause begin as a weighted denial after the conditionals have closed.
topics.reason: The negative particle after the conjunction launches a new declarative clause, and the long vowel gives the denial audible weight.

words.gloss_range: Form IV completed divine dispatch of the Prophet as object, under negated role scope
words.prose: {{ar:أَرْسَلْنَٰكَ}} ({{tr:arsalnāka}}) compresses divine sender and prophetic object into one Form IV perfect verb: “We” dispatch “you.” Under the negation, the completed mission is not erased; rather, the clause denies that the dispatch made the Prophet a {{tr:wakīlā}} over them. The word pivots from the audience’s {{tr:-kum}} outcomes to the Prophet’s {{tr:-ka}} role, and the shift from third-person divine willing to first-person divine sending lets God directly define the boundary. The positive sending formula at 17:105 helps show that the mission verb remains affirmed while 17:54 specializes it by denied role scope; its long {{tr:ā}} cadence also helps slow the final role-denial clause toward {{tr:wakīlā}}.
words.root_gloss_range: sending, dispatching, releasing, and mission-bearing; local clause affirms commissioning while denying delegated control

topics.headline: divine sender and prophetic object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees divine agency and prophetic recipient-role compressed inside one verb.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence mark the verb as first-person plural perfect with the second-person singular object suffix.

topics.headline: commissioning without delegated control
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that sending establishes mission while the following role complement excludes managerial custody.
topics.reason: The verb takes the prophetic object, the authority-domain phrase, and the role complement under negation, allowing the denial to target a commissioned capacity rather than bare dispatch.

topics.headline: Form IV dispatch image
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the Prophet as one dispatched by God into a domain, not as an autonomous initiator there.
topics.reason: V4 supports sending, dispatching, releasing, and message-bearing; local Form IV grammar selects caused divine dispatch.

topics.headline: person shift and mission thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears God move from being described as the one who wills to directly claiming and delimiting the sending.
topics.reason: Contextual rows identify the iltifāt and compare the positive arsalnāka formula at 17:105 with the negated role frame here.

topics.headline: role-clause cadence and pivot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final clause slow and pivot from audience outcomes to the Prophet’s role.
topics.reason: The word is the final-clause pivot verb, and the long-vowel cadence links it acoustically with the closing role noun.

words.gloss_range: prepositional authority-domain over them, selected under the denied wakil role
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَيْهِمْ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhim}}) names the domain over which authority would have applied, then lets the next word deny the role. The preposition selects supervisory overness in this frame, with spatial “over” still supplying the metaphor for authority. The suffix changes the addressees from {{tr:-kum}} people spoken to into {{tr:-him}} people spoken about, and the phrase’s position before {{tr:wakīlā}} makes the audience-domain explicit before the refused office is named. Its final nasal {{tr:-m}} audibly closes the authority-domain before the office is denied. Same-surah {{tr:wakīl}} passages (17:65; 17:68; 17:86) sharpen the contrast between denied prophetic authority and God-centered sufficiency or human lack.

topics.headline: denied authority-domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the issue is authority over the people, not merely presence among them.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence links the prepositional phrase to the denied role noun, selecting an authority-domain reading.

topics.headline: overness as authority metaphor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that spatial overness remains as the metaphor behind denied supervision.
topics.reason: V4 includes spatial and authority senses; local wakīl complementation selects authority while preserving spatial overness as metaphor.

topics.headline: pronoun angle shift
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the same people shifting from direct audience to the domain of prophetic non-authority.
topics.reason: The suffix changes from the earlier second-person plural to third-person plural in the final clause.

topics.headline: same-surah wakil domain thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears this authority-domain phrase inside Surah 17’s wider allocation of wakil authority.
topics.reason: Contextual rows connect the phrase with same-surah wakīl passages at 17:65, 17:68, and 17:86; the sound row marks the boundary before the final role noun.

words.gloss_range: indefinite accusative entrusted-agent role denied at ayah closure
words.prose: {{ar:وَكِيلًۭا}} ({{tr:wakīlā}}) is the closing role noun, indefinite and accusative under negation. The clause denies any entrusted-agent, guardian, proxy, or manager capacity for the Prophet over them; it does not deny his being sent. Because the word belongs to the trust-and-reliance root family, the denial also redirects reliance away from prophetic control and back toward God. Its tanwīn and final {{tr:-an}} cadence leave the refused office ringing as the ayah’s landing point, and the opening {{tr:rabbukum}} with this closing denial frames the verse as an allocation of authority. Same-surah {{tr:wakīl}} references (17:2; 17:65; 17:68; 17:86) make 17:54 the negative human-prophetic instance within a wider trusteeship thread.
words.root_gloss_range: entrusting, agency, trusteeship, proxy, guardianship, and reliance; local clause denies this role to the Prophet over them

topics.headline: indefinite accusative role denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the denial reaching any instance of this capacity, not merely a named office.
topics.reason: QAC marks the noun as accusative indefinite, and attachment evidence treats it as the role or capacity denied in the sending frame.

topics.headline: entrusted-agent semantics
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the denied role is entrusted management or guardianship of outcomes, not ordinary messengerhood.
topics.reason: V4 supports agent, trustee, proxy, guardian, guarantor, entrusting, and relying; local syntax selects the role noun denied to the Prophet.

topics.headline: final closure of sovereignty logic
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the ayah land on what the Prophet is not, after knowledge and will have assigned outcomes to God.
topics.reason: The word closes the ayah, and contextual rows frame the final denial as the landing point of the preceding sovereignty logic.

topics.headline: Surah 17 trusteeship thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees this closing denial as one node in Surah 17’s wider redistribution of wakil authority.
topics.reason: Contextual rows cite same-surah wakīl language at 17:2, 17:65, 17:68, and 17:86 and distinguish prophetic non-guardianship from divine sufficiency or human inability.

topics.headline: boundary pronoun resolution
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the servants of 17:53 into direct address and finally into the third-person domain over which the Prophet is not wakil.
topics.reason: Boundary evidence resolves the pronoun chain from the prior ayah through the current suffixes into the final authority-domain.
